correctness.rationale: The proof enumerates every integer vector of squared norm five as one of two signed-permutation orbits and obtains the exact support function. The polar chamber has two linear inequalities, so vertices have at most two nonzero ordered differences. Every case is solved in rational arithmetic, giving the unique maximizer in each dimension and the exact facet normals. Explicit contact-vertex affine spans prove they are genuine facets; antipodal constraints prove unique incenter. The standalone verifier executed 2916 exact assertions, including all shell vertices for d=5,6,8,9. Finite checks are not substituted for the proof.

value.rationale: The norm-five cubic shell, including the 2016-vertex eight-dimensional Okubo-associated case, is a naturally occurring higher lattice-shell polytope whose orbit count was already published. Its sharp Euclidean inradius and exactly classified facet contacts answer a natural metric geometry question not solved by orbit counts. The dimension-nine switch from coordinate-sparse to fully supported normals, constant radius plateau followed by square-root decay, and exact exponential contact orbit give a structural nontrivial boundary for the whole dimension family.
